narrative.northStar: Four Spots of Color in the Dark
narrative.overview:
A quiet, near-black page (warm paper in light mode) that four saturated spot colors, blue, pink, green and yellow, keep interrupting. The neutrals do the reading work; the spots do wayfinding, brand and life. Each section owns one spot, the brand gradient braids all four together, and four small dots drift in the hero so the page is visibly alive on arrival. The owner's own words set the posture: motion "give[s] it character, and I want my portfolio to stand out," and the gradient is "part of the character/brand."

Density is relaxed and editorial: one centered hero, then left-aligned sections inside a 1152px column with generous vertical rhythm (64px mobile, 96px desktop per section). Type is one family, Geist, carried by weight and size rather than by pairing. Depth is mostly tonal (three background steps per theme), with real shadows reserved for project media and the description card that overlaps it.

Work leads. The first screen carries a featured project with its outcome, and every project's links are visible text buttons, never hover-only. Contact runs through the form, LinkedIn and GitHub; no email address is rendered.
keyCharacteristics: Dark by default (`#09090B` night), warm paper (`#F5F1EB`) as the light theme.
Four spot colors, one per section, with darker text-safe variants in light mode.
A blue-pink-green-yellow brand gradient used as accent only: hero "Problem Solver", the logo "c", the scrolled-nav hairline, the hero card hover border, the footer divider.
Character motion that loops (floating dots, bouncing arrow, pulsing dot, shifting gradient) and yields only to the visitor's `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Pill-shaped actions, gently rounded (8px) cards, one sans family.

rules.name: The Section Owns a Spot Rule
rules.body: Blue is About, pink is Projects, green is Skills, yellow is Contact. The SectionHeader rule, the nav active underline and text, and the section's interactive accents all take that section's spot. Spot color is wayfinding; never swap one section's color into another.

rules.name: The Two Steps Rule
rules.body: Every spot has a vibrant step for fills, dots, borders and icons and a text step for words. Dark mode uses the vibrant value for both; light mode always uses the `-text` step for text (at least 4.5:1 on every paper surface). Text on a vibrant fill is On-Spot Ink, never white.

rules.name: The Brand Braid Rule
rules.body: The blue, pink, green, yellow gradient is brand. It is built from the text steps, so it darkens in light mode on its own. It appears only as an accent: the "Problem Solver" headline span and the logo "c" (shifting over 8s), the 1px hairline under the scrolled nav and above the footer, and the 1px border revealed when the featured card is hovered or focused. Never behind body text, never as a section background, never in place of a section's own spot.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Geist sets every word. Do not introduce a second display face or a mono kicker; weight (400 / 500 / 600 / 700) and size carry the hierarchy.

rules.name: The Balanced Heading Rule
rules.body: h1 to h3 use `text-wrap: balance`; headings are never set in all caps or letter-spaced out.

rules.name: The Work Leads Rule
rules.body: A featured project with its measured outcome sits on the first screen (the hero card), and every project shows its "Live site" and "Source" links as visible 44px pill buttons. The image hover overlay is decoration only, hidden from assistive tech and the tab order.

rules.name: The Tonal First Rule
rules.body: New surfaces step up a background tone and take a hairline border. A shadow is earned only by an element that physically overlaps or lifts off another.

rules.name: The Echo Frame Rule
rules.body: Featured visuals (project media, the avatar) carry an offset outline frame behind them: a 2px border in the section's spot at low opacity (pink 50% on projects, blue 20% on the avatar), shifted 8 to 12px down and to the side, same radius as the visual. It is an outline in the section color, not a shadow.

rules.name: The Motion Is Character Rule
rules.body: The floating dots, staggered hero entrance, bouncing arrow, scroll-triggered entrances, pulsing location dot and shifting gradient stay. Motion yields only to the visitor's `prefers-reduced-motion` setting, never to taste.

dos: **Do** give every new section one spot color from the rotation and pass it to SectionHeader and the nav maps (`sectionColors`, `sectionTextColors`).
**Do** use the vibrant spot for fills, dots, rules and borders, the `-text` step for words, and On-Spot Ink (#0a0a0a) for text on a spot fill.
**Do** keep the brand braid to accents: headline span, logo "c", 1px hairlines, a hover border.
**Do** keep a featured project and its outcome on the first screen, and keep project links visible as 44px pills.
**Do** step surfaces tonally (background, secondary, tertiary) with a hairline border before reaching for a shadow.
**Do** guard every looping or transform animation behind `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** keep text at 12px or larger and secondary text on the muted token, which clears 4.5:1 on every surface in both themes.
donts: **Don't** remove or still the floating dots, the staggered hero entrance, the bouncing arrow, the section entrances or the pulsing dot; the owner rejected the quiet-at-rest pass.
**Don't** flatten the brand gradient to a single solid color; the owner rejected that too ("it's part of the character/brand").
**Don't** put the brand gradient behind body text or use it in place of a section's own spot.
**Don't** render an email address or mailto link anywhere on the page; it draws spam. Contact goes through the form, LinkedIn and GitHub.
**Don't** hide project links behind hover; the image overlay is decoration.
**Don't** set text in a vibrant spot color on paper; vibrant pink, blue, green and yellow fall to 1.67 to 3.14 on the light theme.
**Don't** put white text on a spot fill; use On-Spot Ink.
**Don't** add eyebrow kickers, numbered section labels or mono labels above headings; SectionHeader is the only header pattern.
